{{Quote|The planet Krev Coeur is rich in raw crystalline material&mdash;and there are the forge factories on Nox.|Daegen Lok|<ref name="DotJ6" />}}
'''Nox''' was a [[Factory world/Legends|manufacturing planet]] that was located within the [[Tython system/Legends|Tython system]] of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]] region. The planet was colonized by the non&ndash;[[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] [[Tythan|settlers]] of the planet of [[Tython/Legends|Tython]] more than thirty-four thousand [[Standard year/Legends|years]] before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]. By [[25,793 BBY]], Nox had become a world dedicated to manufacturing goods whose production was hazardous to the environment, and the planet was polluted to such a level that its inhabitants had to live in [[Domed city/Legends|domed cities]]. In 25,793 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|BBY]], the exiled Je'daii [[Daegen Lok]] planned to supply the [[Force Hound]] [[Tau (individual)|Xesh]] with the forge factories of Nox in order for Xesh to construct a [[Forcesaber]] weapon for Lok.

==Description==
Nox was a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] with no [[Moon/Legends|moons]] that was located within the [[Tython system/Legends|Tython system]] of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]] region,<ref name="DotJ0" /> at [[Galactic coordinates/Legends|galactic coordinates]] L-10.<ref name="EAOC" /> The world occupied the third [[Orbit/Legends|orbital]] position around its [[Star/Legends|sun]] [[Tythos]], and it was polluted to such a level that its inhabitants had to live in [[Domed city/Legends|domed cities]] that were supplied with filtered air.<ref name="DotJ0" />

==History==
{{Quote|Daegen will go to Krev Coeur for the crystal."''<br />''"And to the forges on Nox to machine the hilt.|Hawk Ryo and [[Rori Fenn]]|<ref name="Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan 2">[[Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan 2|''Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan'' 2]]</ref>}}
When the non&ndash;[[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] [[Tythan|settlers]] of [[Tython/Legends|Tython]]&mdash;<ref name="DotJ1">[[Dawn of the Jedi: Force Storm 1|''Dawn of the Jedi: Force Storm'' 1]]</ref> the fifth planet of the Tython [[Star system/Legends|system]]&mdash;<ref name="DotJ0" /> [[Second migration|traveled]] to its neighboring worlds more than a [[Time/Legends|millennium]] after<ref name="DotJ1" /> the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[36,453 BBY]],<ref name="DotJItV" /> they colonized Nox.<ref name="DotJ1" /> Nox was a verdant world and it had supported vast forests and complex ecosystems. But settlers had quickly made use of its rich metal deposits and endless wood supplies to build giant smelting plants, extracting 90 percent of the metals used across the system. Over the space of a thousand years, most of the forests had vanished into ash, and with them the creatures they had supported. It had been a merciless despoliation of the planet, but at the time the system had been a new, mysterious frontier, and those brought there by the [[Tho Yor]] were desperate to make a home for themselves.<ref name="DotJItV" />

[[File:Nox_cities.jpg|thumb|left|200px|The domed cities of Nox.]]
By [[25,793 BBY]], Nox had become a [[Factory world/Legends|manufacturing world]], with nearly ninety [[Domed city/Legends|domed cities]] established on the planet dedicated to the production and refinement of ore.<ref name="DotJItV" /> On Nox, products were made whose manufacture was hazardous to the environment, one such product being the [[CRSF27 space freighter]] built by [[Craedos Shipyards]].<ref name="DotJ0" />

When the [[Despot War]] began in earnest across the Tython system, some of the manufacturing cities threw their production power behind the Despot Queen [[Hadiya]], while others supported the Je'daii. The divisions between these cities ran deep, even in the wake of war as multiple domes had been shelled into complete destruction by both sides. [[Greenwood Station]] was the greatest hater of the Je'daii, as the three closest cities to it had all been destroyed by the Order's bombers.<ref name="DotJItV" />

In 25,793 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|BBY]], the exiled [[Human/Legends|Human]] Je'daii [[Daegen Lok]] planned to supply the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Force Hound]] [[Tau (individual)|Xesh]] with the forge factories of Nox in order for Xesh to construct a [[Forcesaber]] weapon for Lok. During their [[Hunt for Xesh and Daegen Lok|hunt]] for Lok and Xesh, the Je'daii team led by the [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] [[Je'daii Ranger|Ranger]] [[Hawk Ryo]] decided to travel to Nox in order to capture the fugitives.<ref name="DotJ6" />

==Behind the scenes==
Nox was first pictured in the entry for Tython in [[The Holonet]] feature of the official website for ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''&mdash;a [[2011]] [[Star Wars video games|massively multiplayer online roleplaying game]] developed by [[BioWare]]. The planet was depicted in a schematic of the Tython system. Since its establishment in [[2008]], ''The Old Republic''{{'s}} website has gone through a number of changes, resulting in the removal of some of the features and images that were originally located there, including the aforementioned schematic. Nox's name and additional information on it were provided in ''[[Star Wars: Dawn of the Jedi 0]]'', a preview issue of the ''[[Star Wars: Dawn of the Jedi]]'' series of [[Star Wars comic books|comic books]]. The issue was published on [[February 1]], [[2012]], and was written by [[John Ostrander]] and penciled by [[Jan Duursema]]. The manufacturing planet was also mentioned in the [[Dawn of the Jedi: Force Storm 1|first]], the [[Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan 1|sixth]] and the [[Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan 2|seventh]] issue of the series&mdash;published on [[February 15]], [[November 28]] and [[December 19]] of the same year, respectively.
